# Psalm 107 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Give thanks to the LORD because he is good — his faithful love lasts forever!

**2** Let everyone the LORD has rescued say so — those he freed from the enemy's grip,

**3** those he gathered from distant lands, from east and west, from north and south.

**4** Some wandered through the desert with no path, unable to find a town to live in.

**5** Hungry and thirsty, they were about to give up.

**6** Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he rescued them from their misery.

**7** He led them down a straight road to a town where they could settle.

**8** Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love and for his amazing works for humanity!

**9** He satisfies the thirsty and fills the hungry with good things.

**10** Some sat in deepest darkness, prisoners suffering in iron chains,

**11** because they had defied God's commands and rejected the counsel of the Most High.

**12** So he crushed their spirit with backbreaking work; they collapsed with no one to help.

**13** Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he saved them from their misery.

**14** He brought them out of the deepest darkness and snapped their chains.

**15** Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love and for his amazing works for humanity!

**16** He smashed the bronze gates and cut through the iron bars.

**17** Some were fools because of the sinful path they chose; their wrongdoing made them miserable.

**18** They couldn't stand the thought of eating anything; they were at death's door.

**19** Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he saved them from their misery.

**20** He sent his word and healed them — he snatched them back from the edge of the grave.

**21** Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love and for his amazing works for humanity!

**22** Let them bring thank offerings and joyfully tell what he has done!

**23** Some set out on the ocean in ships, making their living on the open seas.

**24** They witnessed the LORD's power — his incredible works on the deep.

**25** He spoke, and a violent wind kicked up, driving the waves sky-high.

**26** The sailors were tossed to the heavens and plunged to the depths; their courage dissolved in the crisis.

**27** They stumbled and lurched like drunks — all their seamanship was useless.

**28** Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he pulled them out of their misery.

**29** He calmed the storm to a whisper; the waves went quiet.

**30** They were so relieved when it grew calm! And he guided them to the harbor they were longing for.

**31** Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love and for his amazing works for humanity!

**32** Let them praise him publicly when the people gather, and honor him in the meeting of the leaders.

**33** He can turn rivers into desert and flowing springs into dry, cracked ground,

**34** and lush farmland into salt flats — because of the wickedness of the people who live there.

**35** But he can also turn the desert into sparkling pools and parched ground into flowing springs!

**36** He settles the hungry there, and they build a city to call home.

**37** They plant fields and vineyards and bring in a bumper crop.

**38** He blesses them so they multiply like crazy, and he doesn't let their herds shrink.

**39** But when they decline and are beaten down by oppression, misery, and grief,

**40** he pours contempt on their arrogant leaders and leaves them wandering in a trackless wasteland.

**41** But he lifts the poor out of their suffering and makes their families as numerous as flocks.

**42** Honest people see this and celebrate; every wicked person is silenced.

**43** If you're wise, pay attention to these things. Think deeply about the LORD's faithful love.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **107:4-32**: This psalm tells four stories of people in desperate trouble — lost travelers, prisoners, the deathly sick, and sailors in a storm. Each time: they cried out, God rescued, and they thanked him. It's the universal pattern of the spiritual life.

- **107:29-30**: 'He calmed the storm to a whisper.' Every person who has ever survived a crisis knows this feeling — the overwhelming relief when the chaos finally goes quiet and you reach safe harbor.

— PNEUMA
